item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Anticonvulsant

lookback_source.quote: N0415K1. Anticonvulsant: Check if an anticonvulsant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: The item's own pages state a 7-day observation/look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days) for both N0415K1 and N0415K2. Per the general convention on p. 2-21, the ARD is day 1 of the count, so the window is the ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days. The item pages use both the phrase '7-day observation period' (N0415K1, p. N-8) and, for the Steps for Assessment and Column 1 general instruction, '7-day look-back period'/'7-day observation period' (p. N-6); these refer to the same window.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415K1 if an anticonvulsant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415K1. Anticonvulsant: Check if an anticonvulsant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415K2 only if there is an indication noted for ALL anticonvulsant medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (indication noted) is coded only when Column 1 is checked.

source.quote: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used; Column 1 = check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication’s therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification must be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident’s skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications must be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products (dietary supplements) are not counted as medications for this item.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415Z1, None of the above, if none of the listed medications (including anticonvulsants) were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed reference resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication’s pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that the medication was received by the resident and for the indication of its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident’s medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Primary source review step for both Column 1 and Column 2 coding.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.criterion: For Column 2 (N0415K2), the indication must be an identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician’s (or prescriber’s) assessment of the resident’s condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition box on the N0415 page; establishes that the indication must be documented.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0 pharmacological classification; facilities may wish to identify a resource their staff consistently use.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish") but with an expectation that the coding source is identifiable.

federal.criterion: Assessors may consult the manufacturer's package insert for the medication's pharmacological classification, or work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm classification.

source.quote: Assessors should consult the manufacturer’s package insert, which may contain the medication’s pharmacological classification.

federal.notes: Suggested resource; use of resources is not required for MDS completion (p. N-12).

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied pages for N0415 do not tie the anticonvulsant item to any payment or case-mix classification.
